notes:
Pages opened: Adiabene, Trajan's Parthian campaign, Roman-Parthian Wars, Mesopotamia (Roman province), Roman-Parthian War of 161-166 (five: the budget). A sixth page, Peace of Nisibis (299), was opened only to see whether it names Adiabene (it does not), one over the budget.

Main finding: all eight Cliopatria shapes are verdict wrong. They sit on the Tigris from west of Mosul to Nisibis and Cizre (bounding box 41.18-42.76E, 36.35-37.51N, about 13.7 k km2) and contain neither Arbela (the capital, 44.0E) nor Nineveh, which the page names as the kingdom's capital and later city, between the two Zabs. The corrections are Arbil governorate plus a 60 km circle round Nineveh, with a 40 km circle round Nisibis from 36 to 164. The area check has no infobox figure to compare against.

Disagreements and gaps: (1) Parthian conquest 145-141 BC (Adiabene page, Mithridates I; infobox 'vassal 145 BC to 224') against about 95 BC under Mithridates II in the parthian-empire dossier (me-06-a); Tigranes retaking Adiabene 88-85 BC is likewise only in that dossier (it cites the Tigranes the Great page). (2) Whether Nisibis belonged to Adiabene: Strabo no, Pliny yes; the page's footnote has Artabanus giving it in 36. (3) 260-286: Cliopatria has no shape and the page is silent; the core is carried through (new keyframe adiabene_260, a bridge). (4) The Mesopotamia page says Diocletian conquered 'territory in Adiabene' lost in 363; no land is named and the Peace of Nisibis (299) page lists satrapies east of the Tigris without Adiabene, so nothing is drawn. (5) The end: c. 379 on the Adiabene page against 370 in Cliopatria. (6) The infobox lists the Roman and Sasanian empires as successors with an ambiguous layout; Sasanian is used. (7) 116/117: Cliopatria has no shape for 114-126.

Needs from others: the parthian-empire dossier has the vassal tint for the kingdom (-95..); the roman-empire dossier has no 116/117 Assyria events for Adiabene; the kingdom-of-gordyene dossier (this batch) records the same dependency from the Gordyene side. Kingdom of Hatra and Characene dossiers (me-06-x) would be the neighbours to the south.

(2) 299 loss and 363 gain of the Tigris-to-Greater-Zab land, drawn as the intersection of the core with eu-04's polygon (roman-empire /ledger/107) so the two dossiers share no cell; keyframe 287 split at 299 and 363. The polygon is eu-04's reading and I did not verify it on a page: the Mesopotamia page gives no year and no land for Diocletian's Adiabene, and the Peace of Nisibis (299) page does not name Adiabene. (3) Nisibis 165: conflict with parthian-empire /ledger/59 noted in the event. (4) Pages re-opened for the thin items: Shapur I (silent on 260-286), Corduene (silent on any Adiabene dependency), Tigranes the Great (88-85 BC retaking, 66 BC annexation of conquests, no end date for Adiabene).
